AdminUserItem.description: One account, as every admin endpoint returns it.
AdminUserItem.title: AdminUserItem

AuthenticatedUser.description:
Who just signed in — identity only.

No roles and no permissions: the effective permission union is resolved by
F031's dependency and served by ``/auth/me``. Login answers "here is your
session", not "here is everything about you"; a second round trip after
sign-in is the honest cost of keeping one definition of the access set.
AuthenticatedUser.title: AuthenticatedUser

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Self-service credential change (F030). Both fields are shape-bounded
only — see the module docstring for where the real policy lives.
ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest

MatrixRoleEntry.description: One column of the matrix save: this role, exactly these codes.
MatrixRoleEntry.title: MatrixRoleEntry

MeResponse.description:
``/auth/me`` — identity plus the effective access set (F031).

Extends the login response rather than restating it: the identity fields
are the same four, and one definition of "who is this" beats two that
almost match. ``roles`` are names (the UI displays them; ids belong to the
admin editor, F033), and ``permissions`` is the **expanded union** — a
superuser sees every code's name, never a wildcard, so the frontend checks
set membership and never special-cases a flag. Both lists are sorted, so
responses are deterministic and diffable.

``is_active``/``is_deleted`` are deliberately absent: a session belonging
to a disabled account does not resolve at all (F029), so fields that could
only ever read "true" would be decoration. ``is_superuser`` is served —
the SPA's access model carries an explicit super-admin flag
(``src/config/access.ts``, ARCHITECTURE §6's "explicit super-admin
handling"), and one truthful boolean beats a client that hardcodes
``false`` and re-derives authority from grant-list length.
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

PermissionItem.description: One permission code, as the dictionary and the matrix show it.
PermissionItem.title: PermissionItem

PermissionListResponse.description:
The whole dictionary, sorted by code.

Unpaginated on purpose: the vocabulary is bounded (§6: "add granular
variants only as needed"), the matrix renders every row by definition,
and F038's management table can filter client-side over the full list —
if the dictionary ever grows past a screen, pagination arrives with the
task that needs it, not before.
PermissionListResponse.title: PermissionListResponse

PreferencesResponse.description: Every preference of the signed-in user — and only theirs.
PreferencesResponse.title: PreferencesResponse

RoleItem.description: One role, as the catalogue and the matrix show it.
RoleItem.title: RoleItem

RoleListResponse.description:
The whole catalogue, sorted by name — small and unpaginated on purpose:
a role matrix with more roles than a screen can show is a different
problem, and F036 will meet it then, not the picker now.
RoleListResponse.title: RoleListResponse

RoleRef.description: A role as the directory shows it: what to display and what to submit.
RoleRef.title: RoleRef

SaveMatrixRequest.description:
The atomic save (BP-7.4): every listed role's grant set is replaced in
one transaction. A UI that sends its whole visible matrix includes the
protected `super_admin` column unchanged — the service accepts that and
refuses any actual change to it.
SaveMatrixRequest.title: SaveMatrixRequest

SettingsResponse.description: The effective settings: every registry key, override or default.
SettingsResponse.title: SettingsResponse

UpdateMeRequest.description:
Self-service profile edit (F041, §7.6): the fields a user owns.

**Email is absent on purpose** — it is admin-managed (§7.3, F033), and
``extra="forbid"`` makes a payload that tries anyway a 422 at the unknown
field instead of a silent no-op: the one thing worse than "you cannot
change this here" is "we accepted it and nothing happened".

Absence and explicit ``null`` differ, the F033 convention: an absent
field is untouched; ``"phone": null`` clears the phone.
UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest

UpdatePermissionRequest.description:
Partial edit with fields-set semantics.

A **code rename** is only permitted while no role holds the code (F037's
service rule, C26): every existing grant means "the code as it reads" —
changing the spelling under live grants would silently rewrite what they
authorise. The description has no such weight and edits freely.
UpdatePermissionRequest.title: UpdatePermissionRequest

UpdateRoleRequest.description:
Partial edit with fields-set semantics: absent is untouched, and there
is no way to change grants here — that is the matrix save's job.
UpdateRoleRequest.title: UpdateRoleRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
A partial edit. Absence and explicit ``null`` differ: an absent field
is untouched, ``"phone": null`` clears the phone. The endpoint reads
``model_fields_set`` — the model itself cannot express the difference.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UserListResponse.description:
One page of the directory, with the server's total — the footer count
and the page contents can therefore never disagree (ARCHITECTURE §10).
UserListResponse.title: UserListResponse

get.description:
Every code with its description, sorted — namespace grouping is the
client's presentation concern, the sort order is the contract.

post.description:
A new code confers nothing until a role is granted it through the
matrix save, which enforces the escalation rule (C26) — this endpoint
needs none of its own.

409.description: A permission with this code already exists.
The code is granted to roles and cannot be deleted.
The code is taken, or in use and therefore frozen.

422.description: The new code is not lowercase `resource.action`.

patch.summary: Rename or re-describe a permission code

get.description:
Every role with its grant codes, sorted by name — the picker's options,
the management list, and the matrix's columns all read this one answer.

403.description: Missing roles.manage, or an escalation beyond the caller's codes.

409.description: A role with this name already exists.

422.description: Shape errors or unknown permission codes.

put.description:
Replace every listed role's grant set in **one transaction**.

Validated before the first write; committed once. There is no ordering of
the payload that can leave half the matrix saved, which is the whole
difference from the reference's per-cell PATCH loop (BP-7.4).

403.description: Missing roles.manage, a change to the seed-owned super-admin role, or an edit escaping the caller's own codes.
Missing roles.manage, or the seed-owned super-admin role.

409.description: The role is assigned to users.

403.description: Missing roles.manage, or the seed-owned super-admin role.

409.description: A role with this name already exists.

get.description: Every declared key: its stored override, or the registry's default.

put.description:
Validate every key before the first write, then upsert in one commit;
the response is the fresh snapshot, so no follow-up GET is needed.

422.description: Field-addressable: `loc` names the offending setting key.

get.description:
One page of accounts, newest first by default.

Soft-deleted accounts never appear — they are audit material (F024), not
directory entries. ``total`` counts everything the filters match, so the
table footer can count without lying (ARCHITECTURE §10).

post.description:
Create the account; the response carries the temporary password
**exactly once**, and only when the server generated it (an admin who
supplied one already has it). The account starts ``must_change_password``.

403.description: Missing users.create, creating a super-admin without being one, or granting a role that exceeds the caller's own permissions.

409.description: The email address is already in use.

422.description: Shape errors, unknown role ids, or a policy-refused password.

post.summary: Create an account with a temporary password

delete.description:
Deactivates and marks deleted — the row survives for audit, sessions
end, and the email stays occupied (an account is never silently reborn).

403.description: Missing users.deactivate, or a self/last-super-admin refusal.

409.description: The account is the last active super-admin.

404.description: No such user (soft-deleted accounts answer 404 too).

patch.description:
A partial edit; ``role_ids`` replaces the whole role set when present.

Flipping ``is_active`` additionally requires ``users.deactivate`` — the
router guard cannot know which fields a payload will touch, so the
service raises ``MissingPermission`` and the translator answers the
generic permission 403.

403.description: Missing users.update (or users.deactivate for the is_active toggle), a protected account, an escalation attempt, or a self-change of roles/status.

409.description: The email address is already in use.

422.description: Shape errors or unknown role ids.

post.description:
The recovery path (no email flow exists): a generated temporary
credential shown **exactly once**, a forced change at next sign-in, and
every session of the target revoked (F030's mechanics, reason ``admin``).

403.description: Missing users.reset_password, or a protected super-admin account.

post.description:
Change the caller's own password — the forced first-login flow and
Profile > Security are the same request.

204 with a **fresh cookie pair**: the session that asked is rotated (a
new ID, same family), every *other* session of the account is revoked
(``password_change``), and ``must_change_password`` clears — one commit
in the service. Refusals are field-addressable 422s (wrong current
password, policy violations, new equals current); a wrong current
password is deliberately *not* a 401, which this API reserves for "your
session is over" — a typo must not sign the user out. The current
password is itself throttled (its own bucket, 429 with ``Retry-After``),
because a stolen session must not become a password oracle.

422.description: Field-addressable (loc = body/current_password or body/new_password); no input value is echoed.

429.description: Too many failed current-password attempts; see Retry-After.

post.summary: Sign in and start a session

post.description:
End the session this request presented, and clear both cookies.

Idempotent: no cookie, a junk cookie, an already-ended session — the
answer is the same 204 and the cookies still leave the browser. The
resolution that produced ``context`` is the full one, so a *rotated*
ID presented here trips the same family revocation as anywhere else; a
stale tab is not a loophole, and neither is a thief.

Revoke every live session of the caller's account, this one included.

Distinct from logout in the one way that matters: it acts under a session
(401 without one), so it can revoke "all *my other* sessions" — the
response to "someone may have my credentials". One bulk UPDATE; the
family link is irrelevant here, because every family dies.
post.summary: End every session of the signed-in user

get.description:
Who the caller is, and what the database says they may do — right now.

The answer is computed from this request's resolution of the session,
roles and permissions (F029 re-loads the graph every request), so a role
change made a second ago is already reflected and a revoked one is gone
(BP-6.3f: no cache to invalidate). Deliberately reachable during a forced
password change — this is how the SPA learns the flag is set and where to
route — which is also why it does not ride the gated ``current_session``.

The permission list is the expanded union, superusers included (every
code, never a wildcard): the frontend checks set membership and never
special-cases a flag (ARCHITECTURE §6 layer 3 — UX mirroring the server's
real answer).
get.summary: The signed-in user and their effective permissions

patch.description:
Full name and phone — the fields a user owns (§7.6).

Uses the **gated** `current_session`, unlike the GET: editing a profile is
a regular mutation and the forced password change outranks it (C30). The
response is the same `MeResponse` the GET serves, so a client that just
saved has the fresh identity without a follow-up read.

403.description: Password change pending (regular endpoints are gated).

422.description: Unknown fields (email is admin-managed) or shape errors.
Malformed key, a null value, or an oversized value.
